title: The domain modulus of a curvilinear coordinate is different from the group order of a scalar
summary: Coordinate arithmetic over Fp is modulo p. If the base point G has order n, scalars k and k+n give the same point.
applies: Nonsingular short Weierstrass curves over primes; characteristic > 3
detail: How many points the curve has, how big the subgroup generated by the selected points is, and how many domain elements the coordinates can take are three quantities that need to be distinguished.
boundary: Only by confirming that a certain number is a multiple of the corresponding point order can it be used to unconditionally reduce the entire period in the scalar.
relevance: Avoid mistaking the domain primes given in the question as dot multiplication periods.
